# Requirements Document: Price differentials of changes and cancellations

## Introduction

When a seller asks to change or cancel order items in a paid order, the airline
answers with an offer that carries a price differential: the old price, the
new price, the penalty, the forfeited amount, what the customer pays and what
the airline returns.  The ONE Order implementation guide shows these amounts
in worked examples and never states the formula that links them.  The model
reads the formula from the worked examples, states only the two non-negative
due amounts (the guide's sign for the total is inconsistent), and takes the
case the guide has no example of as a parameter.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/Change/Differential.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-air/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/Change/Differential.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-201

**User Story:** As a seller, I want every change or cancellation offer to state what the customer pays and what the airline returns, so that I can settle the change without working the amounts out myself.

**Rule:** WHEN the airline prices a change or cancellation of order items THE SYSTEM SHALL state the amount due to the airline, the amount due by the airline and a type code that names the outcome. (Lean: `priceDifferential`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. IF the prices, penalty and forfeited amount of a change are not all in one currency THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the change unpriced.
   - ONE-201.1, proven: proven theorem `differential_rejects_mixed_currency`; example `mixedCurrencyChange`
2. THE SYSTEM SHALL give a price differential a type code that names a collection exactly when an amount is due to the airline.
   - ONE-201.2, proven: proven theorem `differential_collects_iff`; example `changeWithCollection`; example `penaltyNettedOrSeparate`
3. THE SYSTEM SHALL give a price differential a type code that names a refund or a value store exactly when an amount is due by the airline.
   - ONE-201.3, proven: proven theorem `differential_pays_iff`; example `cancellationWithForfeit`; example `penaltyNettedOrSeparate`
4. WHEN the seller asks to keep the value of cancelled items for later use THE SYSTEM SHALL type the differential Reusable and set both due amounts to zero.
   - ONE-201.4, proven: proven theorem `respend_reusable`; example `respendCancellation`
5. WHEN the airline prices a change or cancellation THE SYSTEM SHALL make the amount due to the airline less the amount due by the airline equal the new price, less the old price, plus the penalty, plus the forfeited amount.
   - ONE-201.5, open: open theorem `differential_nets`; counterexample `penaltyAboveRefund`; counterexample `respendCancellation`

#### Open question on ONE-201.5

> For every change or cancellation the airline prices, the amount due to the
> airline less the amount due by the airline is the new price, less the old
> price, plus the penalty, plus the forfeited amount.
>
> Open question for the business.  Two cases break it.  When the seller asks to
> keep the value of cancelled items for later use, the guide shows both due
> amounts as zero, while the formula gives the whole refundable value as due by
> the airline; the example `respendCancellation` shows it.  Under the reading
> that waives a penalty above the refundable value, the airline charges less
> than the penalty, so the formula overstates what the customer pays; the
> example `penaltyAboveRefund` shows it.  Should the value held for later use
> count as the new price, and is a penalty above the refundable value collected
> or waived?

### Requirement ONE-202

**User Story:** As a customer, I want a penalty to cost me the same whether it is deducted from what I get back or charged on its own, so that the way the airline collects it does not change what I pay.

**Rule:** WHEN a change or cancellation carries a penalty THE SYSTEM SHALL either net the penalty against the price difference or charge it separately. (Lean: `dueAmounts`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHERE the penalty is netted THE SYSTEM SHALL add the penalty charged to the price difference and state the result as a single amount, due either to or by the airline.
   - ONE-202.1, proven: proven theorem `netted_single_amount`; example `cancellationWithForfeit`; example `changeWithCollection`
2. WHERE the penalty is charged separately THE SYSTEM SHALL add the penalty charged to the amount due to the airline and settle the price difference on its own.
   - ONE-202.2, proven: proven theorem `separate_penalty_added`; example `penaltyNettedOrSeparate`
3. THE SYSTEM SHALL give the customer the same net amount whether the penalty is netted or charged separately.
   - ONE-202.3, proven: proven theorem `net_same_either_way`; example `penaltyNettedOrSeparate`
4. IF the penalty on a cancellation is larger than the refundable value of the cancelled items THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL not leave the customer owing the airline money.
   - ONE-202.4, open: open theorem `cancel_not_owing`; counterexample `penaltyAboveRefund`

#### Open question on ONE-202.4

> A cancellation never leaves the customer owing the airline money: the
> amount due to the airline is no larger than the amount due by the airline,
> when the forfeited amount is part of the old price.
>
> Open question for the business.  Under the reading that collects the whole
> penalty, a penalty larger than the refundable value leaves the customer
> owing the difference.  The example `penaltyAboveRefund` shows it: a 1,000.00
> order with 20.00 forfeited and a 1,000.00 penalty leaves 20.00 due to the
> airline on a cancellation.  Under the other reading the guarantee holds, but
> the due amounts no longer net to the formula of ONE-201.5.  Is a penalty
> capped at the refundable value, or is the excess collected?
